value: Construction can begin only after the permit is issued
The project is considered complete when the Final Inspection result is Pass
inspection_steps.notes: The Submittal Guidelines confirm a final inspection gates project completion but do not describe a multi-step inspection checklist or how to schedule inspections; the city's Online Permit Portal is referenced generally ('Schedule an Inspection' appears as a portal menu item) but its own scheduling process was not detailed on the page read this session.

value.notes: The PV Submittal Guidelines state: 'After you pay the application fee, you will receive a permit number, which will be assigned to Permit Staff within 3 to 5 business days,' then for residential projects 'Initial Plans Review can take 3 to 7 business days before plan check comments or final packaging instructions are given. Resubmittal Reviews can also take another 3 to 7 business days.' The min/max recorded here (3-7 days) represents the Initial Plans Review stage specifically, the closest single figure to a 'permit review timeline'; the full process can take longer if a resubmittal round is needed, and commercial/industrial review windows are longer (12-15 and 10-12 business days) and out of scope for a residential-only record.

eligibility_constraints.notes: San Leandro's PV Submittal Guidelines document does not state a system-size cap or restrict eligibility by property type — it appears to apply broadly to residential PV submittals rather than gating a separate small-system streamlined tier the way some other cities' ordinances do. A separate SolarAPP+-specific eligibility checklist is referenced elsewhere but was not located/read this session. Left null rather than assuming the common 10kW AC/single-family-duplex pattern seen in other cities without direct confirmation for San Leandro specifically.
